```sql
WITH f_orders AS (
    SELECT o.id
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
       AND o.created_at >= %(from)s
       AND o.created_at <  %(to)s
       AND o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
),
lines AS (
    SELECT ol.order_id,
           ol.variant_id::uuid        AS variant_id,
           sum(ol.quantity)           AS qty,
           sum(ol.line_total_cents)   AS rev
      FROM order_lines ol
      JOIN f_orders fo ON fo.id = ol.order_id
     GROUP BY ol.order_id, (ol.variant_id::uuid)
),
by_product AS (
    SELECT pv.product_id,
           count(DISTINCT l.order_id) AS order_count,
           sum(l.qty)::bigint         AS quantity,
           sum(l.rev)                 AS revenue_cents,
           count(DISTINCT pv.id)      AS variant_count
      FROM lines l
      JOIN product_variants pv ON pv.id = l.variant_id
     GROUP BY pv.product_id
)
SELECT p.id,
       p.sku,
       p.name,
       p.brand,
       p.currency,
       bp.order_count,
       bp.quantity,
       bp.revenue_cents,
       bp.variant_count
  FROM by_product bp
  JOIN products p ON p.id = bp.product_id
 ORDER BY bp.quantity DESC, bp.revenue_cents DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De lijnen worden eerst per order en variant samengevoegd, zodat de grote sortering op (product, order) over veel minder rijen gaat. Ook wordt pas na de aggregatie aan `products` gekoppeld, wat kan omdat de FK van `product_variants` naar `products` elke variant aan precies één product koppelt. De types (bigint voor `quantity`, numeric voor de omzet) en de ORDER BY blijven gelijk aan het origineel.
